html:
In January 1846 Ahmad I Bey, ruler of Tunisia, abolished slavery, making Tunisia the first Muslim country to do so by law.

Tunisia sat at the end of trans-Saharan caravan routes, and enslaved Black Africans were sold in Tunis markets. Ahmad Bey was a modernising ruler who looked to Europe and wanted to show his state was a civilised equal. He moved in steps: he banned the export of slaves in 1841, closed the slave market, declared children born to slaves free, and then freed all slaves.

Abolition came before France's own in 1848 and well before the Ottoman world as a whole. Enforcement was uneven, especially in the south, and the practice lingered among some families. For comparison, Saudi Arabia ended slavery only in 1962.
sum: In January 1846 Ahmad I Bey, ruler of Tunisia, abolished slavery, making Tunisia the first Muslim country to do so by law.
